# Procurement

Procurement is one of the key areas of specialty. The regulatory framework for all procurement activities undertaken by the institution are embedded in the Agency’s “Manual of Procedures” (MoP) which is readily available to every member of staff. The Manual is in line with the National Procurement Policy of The Gambia (GPPA Act 2014) and the World Bank Procurement Policies.

The MoP covers the core principles of procurement for works, services and goods and is designed to meet  the core procurement principles of value for money, economy, efficiency, effectiveness, integrity, and fairness and accountability.

The PPA is an act to provide for the establishment, functions, and powers of The Gambia Public Procurement Authority and for the basic principles and procedures to be applied in the public procurement of goods, works, and services, as well as for connected matters. The GPPA has been in existence since the enactment of the 2001 Procurement Act. This Act was then amended in 2014, inspired by the UNCITRAL Model Law for the Public Procurement, and then into GPPA (Amendment) Act 2018 by repeating the major board into a modern state-of-the-art procurement law to ensure that the procurement law meets the standards of international best practices. Procurement is now governed by the new Public Procurement Act, 2022, Public Procurement Regulations Act, 2023, Procurement Policy and Procedures Manual (February 26, 2024), and Standard Bidding Documents. These acts are backed up by government orders, instructions, regulations, and provisions issued from time to time by the GoTG. The Public Finance Act (PFA) 2014 is being revised and aims to integrate several outstanding and emerging issues into the existing legislation the draft law bill was approved by the cabinet in March 2023.

Context and Rationale

33. The country’s public procurement system has suffered from a lack of compliance, an overreliance on single-source contracts, and limited digitalization. Limited transparency, proliferation of single-source tenders, and lack of compliance with procurement regulations hamper effective service delivery and represent a missed opportunity to maximize value for money by promoting competition. To address these loopholes, a new Gambia Public Procurement Act was adopted in October 2022, paving the way for improving the integrity, transparency, and efficiency of the procurement system.30 However, while the new Act is being implemented, public procurement efficiency remains limited and vulnerable to manual processes. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
